paper_title: VisuoThink Empowering LVLM Reasoning with Multimodal Tree Search
caption: (LEFT) The trend of Pass@1 rate on Visual Navigation as the number of reasoning steps increases. (right) The relationship between the Accuracy@1 on geometry problems (Geomverse) and tree width for rollout search. We observe that LVLMs significantly benefit from longer reasoning chains, although the effect plateaus rapidly beyond a certain threshold of reasoning steps. The relationship between performance and tree width exhibits a more complex pattern, demonstrating an inverted U-shaped trend with both GPT-4o and Claude-3.5-Sonnet.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the Pass@1 Rate (%) achieved by two models, GPT-4o and Claude-3.5-Sonnet, across varying numbers of reasoning steps. The x-axis is labeled "Num. of Reasoning Steps" and displays a non-linear scale with discrete tick marks at the values 5, 10, 20, and 40. The y-axis is labeled "Pass@1 Rate (%)" and utilizes a linear scale ranging from 0 to 100, with tick marks at regular intervals of 20. The line representing GPT-4o is a solid blue line with solid circular markers. It demonstrates an upward trend, beginning at a value of 6.5 at 5 reasoning steps, rising to 32.3 at 10 steps, increasing steeply to 77.4 at 20 steps, and ending at 83.9 at 40 steps. The line representing Claude-3.5-Sonnet is a solid light blue line with cross markers. It also follows an upward trajectory, starting at 19.4 at 5 reasoning steps, increasing to 38.7 at 10 steps, climbing sharply to 87.1 at 20 steps, and concluding with a slight rise to 89.2 at 40 steps.
